business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing SaaS

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system founded on English Common Law with local statutory and customary law elements; unitary national jurisdiction without sub-state tax distinctions
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER-Plus Trade and Economic Integration Agreement (in force since 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2022; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2000; International Companies (Registered Agent) Rules; Central Beneficial Ownership Register regulations issued under the AML/CFT Act 2022

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin (e.g., PRC notary office)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter in English for each UBO
Certificate of Good Standing or Incumbency of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

Bilingual (Chinese-English) name clearance consent letter for adoption of secondary Chinese trade name

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and registered-agent clients against the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Samoa FIU domestic designations. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are identified through a risk-based approach and require enhanced due diligence under the AML/CFT Act 2022 and FATF 40 Recommendations. Ongoing re-screening is performed at least every 30 days; adverse sanctions or PEP hits automatically block incorporation and require compliance escalation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry, MCIL Companies Office (Apia); online name reservation e-service at https://www.companiesoffice.gov.ws
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered primary name must be in Latin/Roman script. A Chinese (Sinogram) name may be carried only as an approved dual secondary name filed with the Registrar alongside the Roman-letter primary name. Articles of incorporation may be bilingual Chinese-English with the English text prevailing for statutory interpretation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the Registrar issues a written notice stating the statutory basis. A written administrative appeal must be lodged with the MCIL Registrar within 21 days of the rejection notice; the Registrar must determine the appeal within 30 days. Residual judicial review lies with the Samoa Supreme Court. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately re-submit a revised name; the original reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the prescribed extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An International Company must maintain a registered office and a licensed registered agent physically located in Samoa under section 9 of the International Companies Act 1987. A purely remote or virtual address is not permitted; the standard compliant structure for a zero-physical-footprint SaaS company is to use the registered agent's physical Apia premises as the statutory registered office. No separate office lease is required for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; quantified risk below 5% (0.05) for a low-risk, non-licensed infosec SaaS entity with no cash-intensive activities and records properly maintained at the registered agent. Unannounced physical inspections remain possible if the FIU elevates the AML risk rating or adverse screening results arise.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 of the Independent State of Samoa, as amended by subsequent amending legislation; applicable provisions on the formation of an International Company, registered office and licensed registered agent requirements, memorandum and articles of association, appointment of directors and members, and the statutory exemption of non-Samoan-source income from Samoan income tax.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies, Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Charter) together with the prescribed Application for Incorporation of an International Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or deposit account requirement; the subscriber may adopt a nominal authorized capital (commonly US$10,000) and allot shares without any mandatory cash deposit. Consideration for shares is fixed by the directors under the International Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [INSERT COMPANY NAME] INTERNATIONAL COMPANY

RESOLVED, that the allotment of founding subscription shares is ratified and confirmed, and such shares are fully paid by consideration set out in the subscription agreement.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is established at the office of the Licensed Registered Agent in Apia, Samoa, and the Registered Agent is appointed to act as the Company's local representative.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director Name] is appointed as Sole Director, and [Secretary Name] is appointed as Secretary.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Sole Director and Secretary are jointly authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete filings with the Samoa International Finance Authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registration Unit, Apia, Samoa (submission through a SIFA-licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a SIFA-licensed registered agent and instruct it to submit a name reservation application with three ranked proposed company names. The agent confirms that the selected name is not identical or confusingly similar to any name on the International Companies Register and that no restricted word is included. Submit the prescribed name reservation form together with the agent's due diligence questionnaire on the proposed ultimate beneficial owner and pay the reservation fee.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (prescribed SIFA form)
Registered agent engagement letter
UBO due diligence questionnaire and declarations
Authenticated passport copy of each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the request is rejected or the name is reserved for a conflicting entity, file a fresh reservation with alternative names within 7 days, or submit a written appeal to the Registrar for a binding decision; a refusal may be appealed to the Supreme Court of Samoa where it is plainly erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of Charter Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed registered agent and a notary public in Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association (Charter) conforming to the International Companies Act, incorporating the reserved name, a sole director and single member structure, flexible share capital provisions with no par value shares, and a registered office clause at the agent's Apia address. The subscriber executes the Charter before a notary public, and the notary certifies the execution signature and affixes a notarial certificate to the document.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Charter) in English
Subscriber's executed signature pages
Notarial certificate of execution
Consent to act of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry later objects to any Charter provision as non-compliant, the registered agent files a deed of amendment or a restated Charter; purely typographical or clerical corrections are processed without a supplementary government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Incorporation Application with SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed Application for Incorporation together with the executed Charter, the registered agent's consent, director and secretary consents, and proof of payment of the US$200 incorporation fee by wire transfer to SIFA's official account. The filing may be delivered by courier to the Registry or transmitted electronically through the registered agent's secure portal; the application must confirm the non-resident business purpose and the intended foreign-source revenue model.
required_dossiers: Prescribed Application for Incorporation
Executed and notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent of the Licensed Registered Agent
Consent of the sole director and secretary
Proof of remittance of the US$200 government fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA issues a requisition requesting further information or additional due diligence, the registered agent cures the requisition within 30 days by filing supplementary declarations; no additional fee is charged where the requisition arises from an administrative or evidentiary gap.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registration on the International Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After full compliance, the Registrar enters the Company on the International Companies Register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation dated and sealed by the Registry. The certificate is conclusive evidence of due incorporation. The registered agent then obtains a certified copy of the Charter and register extracts, and issues the registered office confirmation letter for the Company's corporate records.
required_dossiers: Approved Application for Incorporation
Registry receipt of the paid fee
Certified copy of the registered Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed or the Register entry contains an error, the Company submits a written request to the Registrar for a certificate of correction or duplicate certificate; the Registrar rectifies the register as of the original incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolutions, Share Allotment and Statutory Record Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's registered office in Apia, Samoa, through the SIFA-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole director convenes the first board meeting (in person or by virtual means as permitted), adopts the First Board Resolution ratifying the subscriber share allotment, the establishment of the registered office, and the appointment of the director and secretary; the minutes are entered in the statutory minute book, share certificates are issued to the subscriber, and the Register of Members, Register of Directors and Register of Charges are opened at the registered office for inspection.
required_dossiers: Adopted pro-forma First Board Resolution
Register of Members
Register of Directors and Secretaries
Share certificates
Registered agent's acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any statutory register or minute is found defective, the director may pass a confirming resolution and re-execute the contested record; any omitted consent of the director or secretary is completed and annexed to the minute file without penalty if done prior to the first audit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exemption Certification and Corporate Bank Account Formalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (tax exemption administration) and a Samoa-licensed or international bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through the registered agent for the statutory tax exemption certificate confirming that the Company's non-Samoan-source income is exempt from Samoan income tax. Open the corporate operating bank account using the Certificate of Incorporation, the Charter, the First Board Resolution and the UBO's KYO dossier, designating wire transfer capability. Thereafter complete merchant onboarding with Stripe in the Company's name; the execution depends on the payment processor's supported jurisdiction and banking validation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association (certified copy)
First Board Resolution authorizing bank account opening
Tax exemption certificate application
UBO passport, proof of address and reference letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax exemption certificate is not issued within the administrative timeline, the registered agent files a follow-up request and, where necessary, a formal application for administrative review; if the bank or payment processor requests additional KYO or source-of-funds evidence, the director supplies a consolidated KYO packet together with the registered agent's corporate standing certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — Samoa's Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour requires no industrial or manufacturing operating license for a cloud-based cybersecurity SaaS business; an International Company confined to foreign-source services is not subject to the local business license regime and is statutorily prohibited from carrying on a domestic Samoan business.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating, factory or manufacturing permit is triggered; a physical business license would arise only if a domestic branch were established in Samoa, which is outside the International Company structure. The Company relies on its Certificate of Incorporation and tax exemption certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), administering the Planning and Urban Management Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — SaaS vulnerability scanning and penetration testing services involve no physical construction, installation, or land disturbance; the activity is outside the scheduled activities requiring EIA registration or a full EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None triggered — the business has zero wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams from its virtual operations. If the Apia registered office later introduces on-site electronic equipment, resulting e-waste must be disposed of through an authorized waste contractor, and any emergency generator installation would be subject to the applicable national air quality emission standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for the initial virtual SaaS structure. If a physical Apia representative office is established, the Company must obtain (i) fire safety certification from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority; (ii) structural load inspection and building clearance from the Planning and Urban Management Agency for the leased premises; and (iii) occupational health and safety registration under the applicable Samoan workplace safety regulations. None of these clearances is triggered by the Company's remote cloud-based operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Government of Samoa; official tax and customs portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: International Companies (ICs) are not issued a Samoa TIN/VAT ID and are not required to register for taxes because they are statutorily tax-exempt. The standard procedure is: (i) incorporate the International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 with the Registrar of International Companies administered through the Samoa International Finance Authority; (ii) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and maintain a registered office in Samoa; (iii) rely on the automatic tax exemption in section 200 of the International Companies Act 1987; and (iv) if the foreign entity wishes to conduct onshore Samoa taxable activities, it must instead incorporate or register a Samoa domestic company, obtain a TIN from the Ministry for Revenue, and apply for VAGST registration where the WST 100,000 threshold is met or voluntary registration is desired.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime exists in Samoa. An International Company is automatically in the Tax_Exempt_Zone category and cannot elect to be treated as a domestic taxable company, pass-through entity, or hybrid entity under Samoan law. Any onshore taxable activity must be ring-fenced through a separate Samoa domestic company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (compulsory VAGST registration for any person carrying on a taxable activity where taxable supplies exceed WST 100,000 in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is available below this threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate is currently in force in Samoa. Registered persons must issue valid VAGST tax invoices and retain supporting documentation; VAGST returns are filed electronically through the Ministry for Revenue portal. Cross-border SaaS export transactions are not subject to a Samoan tax-authority digital clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAGST Act, a zero-rated export supply requires that goods are exported from Samoa or that services are supplied to a non-resident person and are consumed or performed entirely outside Samoa. For cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration-testing SaaS, the supplier must demonstrate the customer is not a Samoan resident and that the benefit of the service is not enjoyed in Samoa. An International Company, however, is exempt from VAGST by statutory operation, so its export SaaS supplies fall outside the VAGST system entirely and no VAGST zero-rating refund mechanism is engaged.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (required only for physical goods; not applicable to pure SaaS export)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (required only for physical goods; not applicable to pure SaaS export)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Commercial invoice stated at 0% VAGST or tax-exempt status
Underlying SaaS subscription and penetration-testing engagement agreement
Proof of non-resident customer status (e.g., photocopy of passport, certificate of incorporation, or tax residence certificate)
Technical delivery and cloud usage evidence showing the service was delivered from offshore infrastructure and consumed outside Samoa
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may audit export zero-rating and exemption claims, with extension periods for fraud or wilful misstatement. If documentary substantiation is incomplete or false, the claimed zero-rating is denied, the full 15% VAGST is assessed on the supply, refunds are clawed back, and late payment interest plus civil penalties may be imposed. Criminal fraudulent invoicing or false export documentation can result in fines, imprisonment, and retrospective reversal of the International Company's tax exemption where the exemption is used to conceal a domestically taxable activity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa) — the sole monetary authority and exchange-control administrator under the Exchange Control Act 1972, the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is partially convertible rather than freely convertible. Current-account payments — trade in goods and services, SaaS subscription fees, operating expenses, and dividend remittances supported by audited distributable profits — are generally processed by authorised dealers (commercial banks) against standard documentary evidence without case-by-case CBS approval. Capital-account transactions, including direct cross-border investment, intercompany debt, treasury placements, and officer loans, require explicit CBS approval or a standing facility. A Samoa International Company (IC) is treated as non-resident for exchange-control purposes and may hold a CBS-approved Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR/AUD/NZD) at an authorised dealer; SaaS subscription collections can be retained in USD without conversion to WST, and conversion is required only for local Samoan operating costs. Profit-remittance hurdles are minimal where the bank holds the IC registration certificate, non-resident declaration, board resolution, and audited financial statements evidencing distributable reserves; the practical friction is a 3-to-10-business-day exchange-control verification window and the bank's right to require a CBS foreign-exchange application form for each dividend payout.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Exchange Control Act 1972 and the Exchange Control Regulations impose three core rules: (i) a resident exporter must receive full export proceeds from foreign sales of goods or services within a statutory time limit of six months from the date of exportation or performance, unless the CBS extends the period; (ii) proceeds must be surrendered, i.e., offered to an authorised dealer in exchange for WST immediately upon receipt, which in normal banking practice means within 14 calendar days of credit; and (iii) the default mandatory conversion ratio is 100% for ordinary resident exporters without a standing Foreign Currency Account exemption. For a licensed International Company under the International Companies Act 1987, the CBS routinely grants standing approval for an IC-designated Foreign Currency Account, allowing 100% retention of export receipts in USD or another approved currency with no WST conversion; the effective mandatory surrender ratio is therefore 0% for ICs holding such standing approval. Where the IC has not secured FCA standing approval, the authorised dealer treats each receipt as a designated foreign-currency deposit and may require conversion to WST on the full amount. The IC must file export/T-form declarations with the authorised dealer on request, and the authorised dealer submits quarterly foreign-exchange returns to CBS.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Samoa (formerly ANZ Samoa; wholly owned by the Government of Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — USD Foreign Currency Account, IC-designated
Capital Escrow Account — USD-denominated IC escrow with standing FCA approval
Operational Account — USD/AUD Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — legally restricted. Samoa has no EMI or restricted-licence regime for offshore fintech banks; the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and CBS payment-system rules reserve deposit-taking and money-remittance services to CBS-licensed authorised dealers. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and Currencycloud cannot obtain settlement accounts or domestic clearing membership in Samoa, and using them as primary treasury rails would constitute an exchange-control breach, create concentration risk at the local clearing bank, and potentially trigger suspension of the IC's banking relationship. Such EMIs have supplementary viability only for low-value disbursements such as contractor payouts, provided each transaction is mirrored and transparently recorded in the authorised-dealer ledger for compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandated in substance. The CBS AML/CFT Guidelines under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 require authorised dealers to identify and verify every director, signatory, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner. For non-resident ICs, banks require either: (Option A) physical attendance of at least one director or designated signatory at the account-opening interview at the bank's branch in Apia, with original passports and entity/trust documentation; or (Option B) fully remote opening via an encrypted video KYC interview between the compliance officer and all beneficial owners, with wet-signature documents notarised by a Samoa-registered notary or Apostille legalised, supported by the bank's registered-agent relationship. In practice, physical attendance yields a 1-to-2-week onboarding timeline and standard due diligence; remote opening is permitted only under Enhanced Due Diligence with a 3-to-4-week timeline, a higher minimum credit balance, commonly USD 50,000 to 100,000, and a full source-of-funds questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident International Company with indirect trust ownership and nominee directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified IC Registration Certificate from the Samoa International Companies Office; complete register of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners; trust deed, deed of settlement, and letter of wishes; source-of-funds declaration; certified passports of all 25%-or-greater beneficial owners; registered-agent certificate of good standing; two reputable bank references; and a board resolution prepared in compliance with the International Companies Act 1987. The registered agent's AML file must be annexed to the bank's CDD record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border cybersecurity SaaS revenue lacking physical-delivery evidence and transfer-pricing documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master services agreements, statements of work, and engagement letters for vulnerability scanning and penetration testing; itemised commercial invoices tied to subscription licences; Stripe merchant settlement reports showing merchant-of-record branding; evidence of economic substance including a Samoa office lease, employee or contractor agreements, and local management accounts; tax registrations; and an independent professional opinion describing the ISIC 6201/NAICS 541512 digital-services supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction counterparty traffic in payment routing and potential sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed client KYC onboarding files for every contracting counterparty; UN, EU, US/OFAC, and UK sanctions screening results dated within 90 days; IP/export-licence clearances where cybersecurity tooling may trigger dual-use export controls; signed end-user certificates; CBS export declarations; and the bank's required no-prohibited-transaction covenant executed by the IC's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency-derived capital injection or unexplained liquidity above USD 100,000
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Originating bank statements for the sending account; complete chain-of-custody evidence for any crypto-to-fiat conversion executed through a licensed exchanger, including the exchanger's licence and audit report; audited source-of-funds letter from a reputable accounting firm; statutory declaration of net worth signed by each beneficial owner; certificate of prior-year tax compliance; and a written corporate policy prohibiting crypto-origin deposits, adopted by the IC board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid pass-through treasury pattern: Stripe payouts credited and disbursed to third parties within a single day
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adopted treasury and liquidity policy; intraday same-day reconciliation ledger; client purchase-order confirmations and outbound vendor invoices; authorised signatory matrix; outsourced IT and cloud supply agreements matching the disbursement cadence; and a legal memorandum concluding that the IC is operating a genuine SaaS business rather than an unlicensed money-transmission service.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be directed to the IC's USD-denominated Foreign Currency Account at a CBS-authorised dealer, being Bank of Samoa, Samoa Commercial Bank, or BSP, using SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer). The remitter must state the shareholder legal name in Field 50K, the exact registered IC name in Field 59, and a remittance reference in Field 70 that exactly matches the share-register entry, e.g., 'SUB/2025/WS-IC/004 — SHARE CAPITAL'. Field 71A should be 'OUR' or 'SHA' on a conservative basis to eliminate cost ambiguity. For USD wires originating from the US Fedwire system, the beneficiary account must be the standard Samoa account number without IBAN, and the reference must include the token 'IC-WS'. The authorised dealer's compliance pack requires: a board resolution approving the subscription; an updated share register; an issued share certificate; the IC registration certificate; a CBS capital-inflow declaration where the injection exceeds the current-account threshold; and confirmation that the funds are not repatriated crypto-assets. Intercompany loans require a written facility agreement, CBS exchange-control approval, and arm's-length interest documentation to prevent recharacterisation as equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade disbursements for the SaaS business, including cloud hosting, security tooling, subcontractor fees, and platform licences, are cleared through SWIFT MT103 from the IC's Foreign Currency Account in the original invoice currency, USD, EUR, or AUD, with no WST conversion. For institutional-scale procurement or where a vendor requires a bank guarantee of payment, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued under UCP600 via SWIFT MT700 through Bank of Samoa or SCB's international correspondent network is permissible; the LC must describe the service in ISIC 6201 terms, and the presentation must include a commercial invoice, a certificate of service performance for the SaaS milestone, and a certificate of origin where requested. SWIFT GPI tracking is strongly recommended to evidence final value-date credit for AML reconciliation. Key operational controls are: inclusion of the underlying invoice reference in Field 70; independent call-back pre-verification of payee bank details; disbursement thresholds aligned with the AML pass-through defence; and timely quarterly FCA reporting by the bank to CBS.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward contracts (USD/WST) with a CBS-authorised dealer, tenor up to 12 months, covering local operating cost exposure
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD entered into with licensed international banks, cash-settled in USD
Cross-currency swaps between USD and EUR/AUD/NZD using the IC's dual-currency Foreign Currency Account balances, subject to CBS standing approval
Plain vanilla European-style foreign-currency options (USD/EUR, USD/AUD) purchased from qualified dealer banks to hedge vendor payables
Intra-group notional netting on the multi-currency Foreign Currency Account to avoid fragmented FX exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return (Form IR 1) and payment of annual government renewal fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: filing is due within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation; the registered agent issues renewal notices at least 45 days before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of USD 150 or WST equivalent applies immediately; unpaid fees accrue interest while the return remains outstanding. Continued default beyond approximately six months permits the Registrar to publish an intention-to-strike-off notice and dissolve the company after the notice period; directors become liable for filing failures and may be disqualified.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None. A Samoa International Company is not required by the International Companies Act 1987 to prepare audited financial statements or to file financial statements solely because of revenue, assets, employees, or shareholder count. Audit, if any, arises only from constitutional documents, lender/investor covenants, or a voluntary assurance decision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB (or a local GAAP acceptable to the registered agent) may be used for voluntarily prepared financial statements; the Annual Return does not require the attachment of financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Before each Annual Return is submitted, the registered agent obtains a signed UBO confirmation from the directors/shareholders certifying any transfers, declarations of trust, or nominee changes during the preceding year. The beneficial ownership register and statutory registers are reconciled on a line-item basis; any change identified in a share transfer is updated within 14 days. No public UBO filing is made; confidential UBO records are accessible only to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and authorized regulatory bodies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and share-transfer ledgers
Register of Directors, secretaries, and alternate directors
Beneficial ownership register maintained by the licensed registered agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; if voluntarily engaged for investor or banking purposes, approximately USD 2,000 - USD 6,000 for a cybersecurity SaaS holding structure.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income tax exemption for International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987; exempt on all offshore-sourced income, dividends, interest, royalties, and capital gains; annual government fee of approximately WST 1,800 replaces income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No income tax return for exempt International Companies; annual compliance return (Form AR-IC) filed with the Samoa International Companies Registry via online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return and government fee due on the anniversary date of incorporation; registry allows a grace period of 30 days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact registered legal name, company number, date of incorporation, and registered address in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident owners, supply certified copy of passport/ID and a service-of-process address at the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and full Samoa address of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A licensed Samoan registered agent is mandatory; no direct foreign agent address may be used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names, nationalities, residential addresses, shareholdings, and beneficial ownership declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 100% non-resident shareholding is permitted; nominee directors are acceptable but the ultimate beneficial owner must be disclosed to the registered agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-payment of annual fee triggers a late fee of WST 200 plus WST 100 per day, up to WST 5,000; persistent default leads to strike-off and restoration costs.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network. No treaty relief or Tax Residency Certificate process is applicable. Dividends paid from an exempt International Company are distributed without any Samoan withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% for International Companies; standard Samoa withholding tax is 15% for royalties and 15% for interest paid to non-residents under the Income Tax Act 2015.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable to tax-exempt International Companies. Domestic transfer pricing rules apply to active Samoan taxpayers with related-party transactions and annual turnover exceeding WST 20 million; no separate Local File or Master File threshold has been gazetted.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa has not enacted Economic Substance Regulations for International Companies. The tax-exempt status may be challenged under the general anti-avoidance rule if the company is effectively managed or controlled in Samoa or lacks demonstrable offshore economic purpose.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a tax-exempt International Company to conduct active domestic Samoan business while claiming offshore exemption, or willfully omitting taxable income from domestic operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 150% of unpaid tax, interest at 10% per annum, criminal fine up to WST 1 million, and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unpaid taxes attributable to their direction or willful misconduct; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a tax-exempt International Company without legitimate economic purpose, holding undisclosed assets, or misrepresenting beneficial ownership to the Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off, mandatory deregistration, forfeiture of assets, and penalty of WST 20,000 under the International Companies Act 1987 as amended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be disqualified for up to 5 years, personally liable for winding-up debts, and banned from serving in any Samoan-registered entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, keep beneficial ownership records, or report suspicious transactions to the Samoa Money Laundering Authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to WST 300,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018; freezing orders may be imposed on bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers face individual criminal liability, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and disqualification from holding financial services licenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the annual return or pay the annual government fee by the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late penalty of WST 200 plus WST 100 per day; strike-off after three months of default; restoration fees up to WST 2,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for restoration costs and, in cases of persistent default, subject to travel bans and temporary prohibition from serving as officers.
